The Petitioners have filed this petition against Respondents for the relief of compensation under Sec.166 of Motors Vehicles Act, 1989.
SCCH 5 2.

The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 11.12.2023 at about 7.00 p.m. B.R.Manoj Gowda was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51- HU-4097 opposite to Ishwarya Bar, Sarjapura Road,
Bidaraguppe Village, Attibele Hobali, Bengaluru Disrict, at that time, a lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-4720 being driven by its driver ahead of the said motor cycle took sudden left and stopped the lorry without any indication in negligent manner.
Due to the said impact, B.R.Manoj Gowda dashed his motor cycle to left rear portion of the lorry, as a result, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, Manoj Gowda was taken to Oxford Hospital, unfortunately he died on the way to the hospital.
3. At the time of accident, deceased/B.R.Manoj Gowda was aged about 18 years, he was running Cyber Centre at Attibele, thereby earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.
SCCH 5 petitioner No.1 is mother and petitioner No.2 is father of the deceased.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners have lost sole bread earner of the family and they are struggling for their livelihood.

Out of the said accident, crime No.539/2023 is registered against the driver of the lorry bearing Reg.
No.KA-53-D-4720 before the Attibele Police.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is owner of the said offending lorry, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

So that,
prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.54,00,000/- with interest.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.1/insurer has appeared through counsel and filed written statement.
Respondent No.1 seeks protection under Sec.147 and 149 of M.V.Act.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Further submitted that, driver of the lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-4720 SCCH 5 was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the Deepa S vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/73773114/
2 time of accident.

Further submitted that, alleged accident was occurred due to sole negligency on the part of the deceased himself.
Further submitted that, deceased has ridden the motor cycle without having driving licence and without wearing helmet as on the date of accident.

Further denied age,
occupation, income of the deceased and relationship of the petitioners with deceased are also denied.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exaggerated.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
SCCH 5 5.
On service of summons, respondent No.2/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied occurrence of the accident on the alleged place, date and time.

Further submitted that, he is R.C.Owner of the lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-53-D-4720 and all other vehicle documents are standing in his name and the said lorry was insured with respondent No.1 valid from 01.08.2023 to 31.07.2024 and the alleged accident was occurred on 11.12.2023, hence the policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further submitted that, driver of the offending lorry does not possess valid and effective driving licence.
Compensation claimed by the petitioners is on higher side.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this court has framed the following:
SCCH 5 ::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioners prove that, deceased B.R.Manoj Gowda, S/o.
B.K.Ravi Kumar died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.11.2023 at about 7.00 p.m.
near opposite to Ishwarya Bar, Sarjapura Road, Bidaraguppe Village, Attibele, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-53-D-4720 and dashed against the deceased motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so how much and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
7. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.2/father of the deceased himself deposed his evidence as PW-1 and exhibited 9 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.
SCCH 5 8.

Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:

sentences.text: Issue No.1:- In order to prove their case, petitioner No.2/father of the deceased has deposed his evidence as PW-1, in his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in their petition.

In this regard he has exhibited copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2,
copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of inquest report is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of P.M. Report is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of SCCH 5 charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7 and copy of sketch is marked as Ex.P.8.
10.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and the records those were marked i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, IMV Report, inquest report, P.M.Report, charge sheet and sketch corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 11.12.2023 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, though respondents have appeared and filed written statement, but they have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of B.R.Manoj Gowda out of the accident held on 11.12.2023 at about 7.00 p.m. when he was riding motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-HU- SCCH 5 4097 opposite to Ishwarya Bar, Sarjapura Road, Bidaraguppe Village, Attibele Hobali,
Bengaluru District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the lorrY bearing Reg. No.KA-51-HU-4097.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/B.R.Manoj Gowda was aged about 18 years as on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased, SCCH 5 they have produced copy of aadhar card of the deceased marked as Ex.P.9, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 29.09.2005, the alleged accident was occurred on 11.12.2023.

Accordingly relying on aadhar card,
age of the deceased is considered about 19 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 18 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

16. As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the deceased is bachelor, then 1/2 of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/2 of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,

No.KA-53-D-4720 has issued insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 vide policy bearing No.2315 2055 8040 9600 000 which is valid from 01.08.2023 to 31.07.2024, the alleged accident was occurred on 11.12.2023, hence as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.

So that,
respondent No.1/insurer of the lorry is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
SCCH 5 ::ORDER::
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,75,800/- (Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Seventy Five Thousand Eight Hundred Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
